author: WP11
summary: Contrasts the three non-GPU renderers as test doubles: HEADLESS validates and traces, SOFTWARE rasterises a bounded subset, STUB does nothing, with a table of invalid inferences and a capability-discipline lesson. The alpha.1-era description of SOFTWARE and of HEADLESS render-target binding is contradicted at 009d40f5. libcna.com already covers all three in depth (three internals pages, Tutorial 107, the validation guide and the capability deep dive), so no new page was needed.

sections.heading: A query result that is not an occlusion measurement
A useful reference with known semantic limits
Choosing the right non-GPU test double

concepts.text: HEADLESS, SOFTWARE and STUB all run without a GPU but answer different questions: whether calls and lifetimes form a valid trace, what a CPU rasteriser draws, and whether framework code survives a renderer that does almost nothing.
tokens: They are not four flavours of the same thing

target.evidence: the three families' descriptors and SupportsCapability

concepts.text: The overview table gives SOFTWARE no MRT and no queries and HEADLESS no MRT with only a trace target.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 SOFTWARE binds up to four targets and counts occlusion samples, and HEADLESS binds MRT sets; the site states the current facts.

target.evidence: modules/renderers/software/src/SoftwareRenderer2DState.cpp (SupportsCapability: MRT, OcclusionQuery true); modules/renderers/headless/src/HeadlessRenderer.cpp (SetRenderTargets binds a set)

concepts.text: HEADLESS builds resource objects, validates arguments and sequencing, records state and draw events, exposes counters and a trace log, and never rasterises; its targets are bookkeeping objects whose bind transitions can be inspected.
tokens: never execute vertex or fragment programs

concepts.text: HEADLESS can prove primitive counts, bound targets, textures and state sequences but not coverage, sampling, blending, depth or final colour.

concepts.section: A query result that is not an occlusion measurement
concepts.text: The HEADLESS occlusion query always reports one visible pixel, a control-flow value, never a visibility or sample measurement.

concepts.section: A query result that is not an occlusion measurement
concepts.text: HEADLESS's capability switch falls through to true for MRT and occlusion queries, which simulates API reachability rather than hardware capability; callers requiring real behaviour must not infer it from the bit.
concepts.note: The source said setting more than one target throws; HEADLESS now binds a whole set, and the site's explanation of the permissive answers is current.

target.evidence: HeadlessRenderer.cpp (SupportsCapability default true; SetRenderTargets binds sets)

concepts.text: SOFTWARE is a real CPU rasteriser covering sprites and a bounded 3D path: lists, strips, lines and points, depth and stencil, multi-stream fetch, texture and sampler state, stock effects and blend factors and equations.
concepts.note: The source listed triangle lists only; the site's current boundary table is broader and correct.

concepts.text: SOFTWARE's stock lighting and fog were outside its first surface, and source text given to SoftwareEffectRenderer is never executed as a custom shader.
tokens: Your GLSL does not run here
concepts.note: Lighting and fog are implemented at 009d40f5; the custom-shader refusal still holds and is stated on the site.

concepts.text: SOFTWARE leaves RenderTargetCube, Texture3D, instancing, MRT and occlusion queries outside its surface, answers false for Texture3D and instancing, and overclaims MRT and queries through its default branch.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 all of these are implemented and answered true explicitly; the claim is not carried over.

target.evidence: modules/renderers/software/src/SoftwareRenderer2DState.cpp (SupportsCapability: Texture3D, Instancing, OcclusionQuery, MultipleRenderTargets true with implementations)

concepts.text: A SOFTWARE screenshot is genuine pixel evidence for the CPU algorithm, not for GPU precision, driver shader compilation, MSAA resolve on hardware or a programmable effect path.
tokens: A Software pass proves its CPU implementation, not hardware parity

concepts.section: A useful reference with known semantic limits
concepts.text: SOFTWARE's deterministic buffers make it a strong local oracle for geometry, streams, sampling, targets, depth, stencil and blending, but only inside its implemented subset; measured against the XNA corpus it is not pixel-exact everywhere.
concepts.note: The source excluded lit, fogged, instanced and cube-target scenes; those are implemented now, and the site gives the dated oracle measurement instead.

concepts.text: STUB keeps no observable rendering state: it creates no render targets, records no trace, its extended draws end in no-ops, and it answers false for every capability.
tokens: silent no-op rather than a refusal

concepts.text: STUB is a teaching device that shows which renderer hooks must exist for the framework to run, and it exposes accidental assumptions such as dereferencing optional factories.
STUB is not a headless rasteriser; a passing STUB lifecycle test proves only that the framework did not demand more than the minimal contract.
tokens: It does not inspect pixels, count draws or validate anything

concepts.section: Choosing the right non-GPU test double
concepts.text: Use HEADLESS for call shape, order, counters, lifetime and validation, SOFTWARE for pixels inside its raster vocabulary and STUB for framework survival, and name the invalid inference each forbids.
tokens: Backend state correctness, resource data, pixel output or GPU lifetime

concepts.section: Choosing the right non-GPU test double
concepts.text: No non-GPU renderer can measure occlusion: HEADLESS returns a constant and SOFTWARE has a null query factory.
concepts.note: SOFTWARE's occlusion query counts surviving samples at 009d40f5; the site states this in the CPU-renderer tutorial.

target.evidence: SoftwareRenderer2DState.cpp (OcclusionQuery true: counts samples surviving coverage, alpha, depth and stencil)

concepts.text: Documentation and tests should name the observable, not only the method: a target can be a trace object or a pixel buffer, a query a control-flow token or a sample count, a draw a log record, a CPU raster or a no-op.
tokens: the pixel, query or structured oracle

concepts.text: The three families illustrate the default policy: STUB overrides everything false, SOFTWARE overclaims features it does not own, HEADLESS lets validation objects look like pixel capability.
concepts.note: SOFTWARE no longer overclaims: its answers are authored and backed by implementations; the STUB and HEADLESS halves are preserved on the internals pages.

issues.text: HEADLESS reports OcclusionQuery true while its query always answers one visible pixel.
The alleged SOFTWARE overclaim of MRT and occlusion queries is absent: both are implemented and answered explicitly.
